title: Upward feedback prep: growth scratchbook
content:
Purpose: quick, messy prep for my upcoming 1:1 with Maya (skip-level). Use as a source of specific evidence + concrete asks. Keep this lightweight — it's a scratchbook, not formal.

Agenda I want to cover (30 min):
- 3 wins I want visible (30s each)
- One area I'm actively developing (30s)
- Specific asks / blockers (5–7 min)
- Career signal + calibration question (5 min)
- Next steps / follow-ups (2–3 min)

Quick summary headline:
- Built and shipped two onboarding experiments that meaningfully reduced TTO (time-to-onboard) and increased new-hire enablement; starting to run cohort-level metrics rather than anecdote-based feedback.

Wins (concrete evidence):
1) Onboarding async course pilot (cohort A, n=18)
   - Metric: average time to first PR reduced from 7.2 days -> 4.9 days (median 3.8). Source: onboarding cohort tracker (JIRA-PO-2374).
   - Qualitative: three managers flagged clearer expectations in first week; saved ~6 hours of shadowing per new hire.
   - Next step: scale to two new cohorts in Q2; request: +1 engineer for 8 weeks to build automations.

2) Offer-to-accept rate improvement (experiment: clearer comp/relocation FAQ)
   - Offer acceptance increased from 72% -> 82% for IC-level hires in EMEA (small n; signal worth validating).
   - Evidence: HR pipeline spreadsheet; anecdotal feedback from recruiting.
   - Ask: greenlight a brief candidate experience survey to run for next 30 offers.

3) Manager enablement playbook beta
   - Internal usage: 9 of 12 managers used the playbook in Feb; managers reported higher confidence for first-quarter calibration.
   - Evidence: manager survey (n=12) average confidence improvement +0.6 on a 5-pt scale.
   - Next step: tidy playbook based on 1:1 notes and ship as canonical doc in Confluence.

Area I want to develop (weakness + plan):
- Stakeholder influence: tendency to over-index on data and small-sample signals; can miss the narrative framing needed for exec buy-in.
- Plan: practice concise decision memos (one-pager: context, decision, request, risks) before any exec discussion. Goal: produce 3 memos and get feedback.

Career signal (where I want to be in 12 months):
- Move toward leading a cross-functional program (ops + recruiting + eng productivity) owning onboarding end-to-end and demonstrating measurable cost/time savings.
- Evidence to collect: cohort-level time-to-first-merge, hiring funnel conversion lift, new-hire NPS.
- Calibration question for Maya: "If I can show sustained reduction in TTO and early-path retention, what additional responsibilities would signal readiness for a Sr. Program Lead role?"

Concrete asks for this 1:1 (prioritized):
1) Permission to reallocate one contract PM for 10 weeks to help with the automations backlog (cost estimate attached in Confluence).
2) OK to run a 4-question candidate experience pulse after offers (needs legal/retention check — will coordinate with Recruiting).
3) Help advocating for clearer org-level signal on new-hire success metrics (request 10–15 min on GTM weekly to align with Eng Productivity lead).

Risks / unknowns: 
- Small sample sizes. Need to be explicit about confidence intervals and plan for rolling validation.
- Bandwidth: current team bandwidth limited — if we over-commit we'll lose momentum.
- Stakeholder fatigue: multiple small asks across teams (recruiting, legal, eng) could slow progress.

Evidence snippets to mention (copy-paste friendly):
- "Time-to-first-PR median: 3.8 days (cohort A) vs 6.9 baseline; p<0.1 but small n (18)."
- "Manager playbook usage: 9/12 managers; average confidence +0.6 on 5-pt scale (survey id: CONFLUENCE-PO-512)."
- "Offer acceptance EMEA (IC hires): 82% post-FAQ vs 72% baseline — next step: run a control for next 30 offers."

What I want Maya to walk away with:
- Clear sense of impact and momentum (we're getting traction on measurable onboarding improvements).
- A short-term resource approval (contract PM or engineering help) to secure momentum.
- A sense of how this maps to my career path (what signals I should prioritize).

Preparation TODOs (self):
- [ ] Draft one-pager for each ask (2x one-pagers): automation + candidate pulse (due: 2026-03-13).
- [ ] Pull cohort-level raw metrics and snapshot charts (due: 2026-03-11). Link: JIRA-PO-2374.
- [ ] Add short bullets to playbook changelog about manager feedback (due: 2026-03-12).
- [ ] Quick run-through with Aiden to trim memos to 1 page (scheduled: 2026-03-09 done).

Notes-to-self (rambling):
- Keep the 1:1 crisp — use metric bullets first then human story. Execs care about scale and risk, managers care about day-to-day.
- Don't bury the ask. Always end with "I need X and here's the tradeoff."
- Be explicit about uncertainty; prefactor with "pilot-sized evidence, plan to validate" so they don't assume finality.

Follow-up and measurement plan if asks approved:
- Automations: baseline TTO, target -25% in 6 months, fortnightly check-ins with engineering.
- Candidate pulse: track acceptance rate and free-text feedback for 60 days.
- Manager playbook: track monthly usage and manager confidence metric (survey n>20 for Q2).

Timestamped log (for my own records):
- 2026-01-18: initial idea notes & pilot plan.
- 2026-02-06: cohort A run completed; basic metrics in tracker.
- 2026-02-20: manager playbook beta shared.
- 2026-03-09: memo drafts reviewed with Aiden.
- 2026-03-10: this doc updated for Maya 1:1.

End of scratchbook — save as reference and prune after 1:1.
